content.title: How to get Netflix for free — here are 3 ways
content.text: When you buy through links on our articles, Future and its syndication partners may earn a commission.Credit: ShutterstockIn 2026, Netflix is still very much the leader of the streaming wars. The streaming service boasted 301.63 million paid subscribers worldwide as of the fourth financial quarter of 2024 alone and continues to draw new users in 2026 thanks to its excellent catalog of original movies like"KPop Demon Hunters" and series like "Wednesday".Despite being a massively popular service — or, more likely, because it's so popular — Netflix doesn't offer many deals or discounts. In fact, you can typically count on Netflix to raise prices over time instead of lower them. Case in point: the streamer only recently announced an additional price hike that viewers will have to eat.Netflix has chosen other methods of boosting subscriber numbers since it does tend to raise its prices often, such as adding a lower-cost ad-supported plan and cracking down on password sharing.But if you have your heart set on getting free or discounted Netflix, it's not impossible if you know where to look. Here are just a few ways that you can get Netflix for free.Is there a Netflix free trial?Unlike most other major streamers, Netflix does not typically offer a free trial. The company discontinued all free trials in the U.S. back in 2020 and is not expected to bring promotional trial periods back any time soon. That means you'll have to be clever about trying the service out.Those looking to get a very small taste of Netflix’s most popular series can only do so via YouTube, where the streamer has a curated collection of full episodes of selected shows like "Blue Eye Samurai," "Explained" and "Our Planet." There, of course, you don't have to pay to sample Netflix's wares.T-Mobile’s 'Streaming on Us' Netflix freebieT-Mobile’s long-running “Netflix on Us” freebie is still available, but it went through some changes earlier this year. Previously, T-Mobile users on more expensive mobile plans like Magenta Max were able to get ad-free Netflix Standard plans.However, that option was officially retired in January 2024 when the company downgraded all customers to Netflix’s ad-supported tier, Netflix Standard. Not only does this mean unskippable ads, but much of Netflix's film library is unavailable on this tier due to licensing restrictions. So if you want to see everything the service has to offer, you'll have to cough up some extra cash.Still, it's free Netflix, which is not nothing, and being able to stream new seasons of "Squid Game" "Emily in Paris" and "Bridgerton" for the low cost of nothing at all is still pretty appealing for those looking to save on streaming. You also get unlimited access to a selection of video games on the service.Learn more at T-MobileVerizon’s Netflix + Max (with Ads) bundleVerizon offers a $10 monthly subscription bundle that includes the ad-supported tiers of HBO Max and Netflix through its myPlan service. Though this might not technically be “free,” the cost of an ad-supported Max subscription on its own is $9.99 per month, so subscribers technically are getting Netflix at no extra cost with the purchase of a Max subscription through Verizon. You're eligible for this bundle, which saves you about $8, if you subscribe to select mobile or home internet plans.Learn more at VerizonComcast 'StreamSaver' bundleIn May 2024 Comcast announced a new “StreamSaver” package that includes Netflix, Peacock and Apple TV Plus all for a “vastly reduced price [when compared with] anything in the market today.” The bundle is exclusively still available as of 2026 to Comcast broadband, TV and mobile customers.The deal is pretty straightforward. You get 150 Mbps internet for one year with Peacock Premium with ads, Apple TV+ and Netflix Standard with ads for $45 monthly.Existing Xfinity internet and TV customers can pay an additional $15 per month for Peacock (with ads), Netflix (with ads) and Apple TV+. That represents 40% off in savings. Comcast Now TV customers will need to pay $30 per month for the same bundle.What streaming services offer free trials?While Netflix may not offer a free trial in the traditional sense, many of the best streaming services actually do. Here is a list of the popular streaming services that you can try for free while you decide whether or not to add Netflix to your streaming budget:FAQsHow much is Netflix a month?If you want to take out Netflix, the entry-level plan costs $7.99 per month for ad-supported viewing. You can watch on two devices, download on two devices and stream in Full HD. If you're curious how much Netflix costs without ads, it's $17.99 per month for the Standard plan. There's also the Premium plan, which allows you to stream on four devices, download on six, and stream in 4K for $24.99 per month.How do you cancel Netflix?If you want to cancel your Netflix subscription, you need to log into your account on the web or app, click or tap the profile icon at the top right of the screen, navigate to Account > Cancel Membership and select Finish Cancelation.Does Netflix have a student discount?Netflix doesn't offer a student plan or student discount. If you're a student looking to save, the best way to do this is to have one member of your household take out a Standard or Premium membership, create dedicated user profiles for each person, and split the cost of the plan each month.More from Tom's Guide
